fix(network): cancel abandoned geocoder requests, and stop a truncated payload drawing NaN

Search kept a sequence number but not the request: the number could stop an old
answer from being painted, while the download it was waiting for ran to its 9s
deadline and then on to the second geocoder. Typing "mum", pausing, then
finishing "mumbai" left two requests in flight and up to 18s of radio time for
an answer nobody would see; closing the sheet bumped the number and left the
request running. Search now owns an AbortController - a new query, a shorter
one, or a closed sheet cancels the previous request - and an abandoned query no
longer falls through to the Nominatim fallback, which it did because aborting
the first request threw out of the try straight into the second service.

usableForecast() checked the three numbers behind the hero and took the rest on
trust: a body cut before wind_gusts_10m rendered "gusts NaN" in the wind card,
and an hourly block cut short of the current hour rendered eight "NaN" cells in
the hourly strip (the hourly arrays were only tested with Array.isArray, never
for the length of hourly.time, while the daily block had that check all along).
Every field the cards and the strip index is now required, so a truncated
payload is rejected before it is cached instead of being drawn.

Verified: node --check clean, zero console errors on load and through a full
interactive pass, byte-identical #main/#nav markup and 0 differences across 126
computed-style checks against 1.5.2. "mum"/"mumbai" 700ms apart: 2 requests
started and 0 cancelled on 1.5.2, 2 started and 1 cancelled on 1.5.3;
superseded while the first geocoder was still thinking, 4 geocoder requests on
1.5.2 and 3 on 1.5.3; sheet closed with a search in flight, the request now
cancels instead of running to its deadline. Body without wind_gusts_10m: "gusts
NaN" on 1.5.2, none on 1.5.3; hourly block of 8 hours: 8 "NaN" cells on 1.5.2,
none on 1.5.3; a payload with no hourly block at all behaves as before.

versionCode 27 / versionName 1.5.3, same signing key. Built by this workflow:
android/assets/index.html and the copy inside the APK both match web/index.html
byte for byte, and CHECKSUMS.txt carries the new digest.

Landed through CI because the audit sandbox can only read the repository.
